action: Check any GTA VI offer on Rockstar's official channels and have HR confirm any corporate giveaway before clicking or scanning a QR code, as KnowBe4 advises.
date_note: Date of the Expansión article relaying KnowBe4's research; the research publication date was not stated.
exec: Staff may receive fake GTA VI giveaways at work or on personal phones; KnowBe4 advises HR confirmation of any corporate offer.
geo_basis: country-level pin; the article names the United States as the most-targeted country
plain: Security firm KnowBe4 says scammers are using fake GTA VI bonuses of up to $4,000 and free-game offers to steal account and card details.
summary: According to a KnowBe4 Threat Lab investigation relayed by Expansión, phishing emails tied to video games rose 1,300% against the March to August 2026 monthly average. Lures offer fake GTA VI bonuses of up to $4,000 and lead to fake pages that collect account passwords or card and crypto-deposit details. Corporate variants offer free copies to the first 250 employees using lookalike domains and QR codes.
title: KnowBe4: GTA VI phishing lures offer fake bonuses of up to $4,000

validation.note: Single publisher (Expansión) relaying KnowBe4's research; KnowBe4's own report was not read.

review.note: Compared 1,300% vs March-August average, up to $4,000, first 250 employees, QR codes, HR advice against Expansion article of 19 Nov
